correctness.rationale: A direct induced-P4 characterization for two cliques connected by a matching yields an iff cograph criterion: no selected bridge, at most one vertex on one shore, or two complete matching pairs. These cases are counted with an explicit overlap subtraction for the full polynomial. Maximality forces each bridge-free pattern to orient every matched pair and include all unmatched vertices; only t+1 boundary orientations are excluded per saturated clique, and these exclusions are disjoint for t>=3. The bridge-containing maximal cases are full-clique plus matched singleton, or two complete matched pairs. The proof covers every integer 3<=t<=min(a,b). Independent graph-level enumeration within the present package checked 57 instances and 320832 subsets, agreement for every coefficient; it is corroboration, not an infinite certificate.

originality.rationale: The closest complete primary treatment (Brosse et al., arXiv:2007.01031, Section 4) proves polynomial-delay enumeration of maximal induced cographs in arbitrary graphs, but not the closed coefficient polynomials for two cliques joined by a matching or the complete-prism size gaps. Cao (arXiv:2004.09885) gives broader algorithmic enumeration results for hereditary graph classes, without the present family-specific counts. Matching-deleted complete bipartite and rook-graph literature identifies the graph families or different invariants; no inspected source states an equivalent enumeration theorem. Research-database searches did not reveal a covering claim, but an unindexed equivalent remains possible, so priority is provisional.
residual_risks: An equivalent graph-family census might appear in an unindexed article or under a different name; absence from searches is not proof of novelty.
The comparison with the general enumeration literature supports non-implication of the explicit formulas, but publication priority has not undergone independent verification.

value.rationale: Cograph vertex deletion is a canonical hereditary-property enumeration problem. The theorem gives complete cardinality multiplicities, not just scalar extremal sizes, for an infinite three-parameter co-bipartite matching family. A boundary correction changes the maximal-set count when a clique is entirely matched. In its connected vertex-transitive complete-prism specialization, maximal cographs have only sizes 4,n,n+1 for n>=6, with n-5 consecutive missing intermediate sizes and asymptotic concentration at n. This structural and distributional information is not an automatic consequence of general listing algorithms.
